It sits inside the university's Tough Cyber-Physical AI Research Center and uses the university's co-creation lab program, which lets companies place research bases on campus.

The focus is what they call tough physical AI. Physical AI is AI that is built into robots and machines and moves in the real world, rather than producing text or images on a screen. According to news reports, the aim is to respond to the construction industry's labor shortage and to frequent natural disasters, and the results will be tested on Obayashi's sites on the way to practical use.

Experts from a wide range of fields will take part, including physical AI, civil engineering and architecture, human-robot collaboration, 3D concrete printing, urban planning, law and ethics, and disaster science and recovery. The lab is set up for five years, until the end of October 2031.
en.commentary: A robot in a factory and a robot on a construction site. They may both be robots, but their surroundings could not be more different. In a factory, the floor is flat and parts always arrive at the same spot. A construction site changes shape every day. Where there was a floor yesterday, there's a hole today. When it rains, the ground turns to mud, and the place where materials are stacked changes from day to day. At home, it would be like running a robot vacuum in a room where the furniture gets rearranged every morning. I read the word “tough” in the lab's name as a goal: machines that keep working in rough conditions like that, and at disaster sites too. The other thing that stands out is that law and ethics are on the list of fields. When a heavy machine makes its own decisions and moves near people, who is responsible if there's an accident? We've reached the stage where the rules have to be written as fast as the technology. Five years from now, I wonder how close we'll be to seeing robots on every site as a normal sight.
briefing: Tohoku University's co-creation lab program is an industry-academia scheme in which a company sets up a research base inside the university and works with university researchers on research, development and training.
The lab's stated goals are to carry out research and development of tough physical AI, train highly skilled people and create new technologies, all as one effort.
Energy is also among the participating fields. Specific research themes and the size of the budget have not been made public, as far as could be confirmed in searches.

hojosen.title: Contractors and site robots
hojosen.body: Japan's major general contractors are competing to use robots on site as they face labor shortages. In October 2026, Shimizu Corporation announced an investment in a US humanoid robot startup. Obayashi itself has built 3dpod, a building made with a 3D printer that meets Japan's Building Standards Act.

hojosen.title: Why Tohoku University
hojosen.body: As a university in the region hit by the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake, Tohoku University has put particular weight on disaster science and recovery research. Disaster science and recovery being among the lab's fields follows from that. Machines that can work in place of people at disaster sites are as important a theme for construction companies as everyday building work.

stories.title: 津田沼パルコ跡地に高さ160mのタワマン 習志野市・船橋市が「特定街区」の都市計画素案
stories.summary: 津田沼駅北口のパルコ跡地で、習志野市と船橋市が都市計画の素案をまとめました。高さは40mと160mの2街区で、27年度の決定をめざします。
body: 千葉県のJR津田沼駅北口にあった「津田沼パルコ」の跡地について、習志野市と船橋市が、再開発のための都市計画の素案をまとめました。敷地を二つの街区に分け、建物の高さの上限をA街区は40メートル、B街区は160メートルとする内容です。
報道によると、パルコA館の跡地にあたるA街区には6階建ての商業・オフィスビルを、B街区には低い階に商業施設が入る40階程度のタワーマンションを建てる計画です。敷地は二つの市にまたがっているため、両市が足並みをそろえて都市計画の手続きを進め、2027年度中の決定をめざします。
パルコの閉店後、A館跡地では三井不動産レジデンシャルが10月1日、本格的な開発までの間の暫定活用として駅前広場「ATOCHI」を開いています。今回の素案は、その先の街の姿を初めて数字で示したものです。
stories.commentary: 駅の南と北に、同じくらいの高さの塔が向き合うことになりそうです。北口のB街区の上限は160メートル。南口に建つ超高層マンション「津田沼 ザ・タワー」と、ほぼ同じ高さです。今回使われる「特定街区」は、少し変わった仕組みなんです。ふつう建物の大きさは、用途地域ごとに決まった容積率、つまり敷地の広さに対して床をどれだけ積めるかの上限で縛られます。特定街区では、その街区だけの専用ルールを都市計画で決めて、高さや容積を個別に設定します。洋服で言えば、既製服のサイズ表ではなく、その体に合わせて仕立てるオーダーメイドに近いんですよね。今回は、A街区を低く抑え、B街区を高くする組み合わせです。低いビルの側とタワーが立つ側を、はっきり分けた配分になっています。もう一つ珍しいのは、敷地が船橋市と習志野市の境をまたいでいることです。一つの建物のために、二つの市が同じ都市計画を同時に決める。決定の目標は、2027年度中です。
briefing: 報道によると、両市のスケジュールでは、早ければ2028年度にA街区の新築工事に着手し、2031年度の完成を想定しているとされています。B街区の着工時期は、検索で確認できた範囲では示されていません。
B街区の高さ160メートルは、駅の南口にある超高層マンション「津田沼 ザ・タワー」とほぼ同じ高さだと報じられています。駅の南北に、同じくらいの高さの塔が向き合う形になります。
A館跡地の駅前広場「ATOCHI」は、三井不動産レジデンシャルが将来の開発までの期間を暫定活用する取り組みとして、2026年10月1日に開業しました。

hojosen.title: 特定街区とは
hojosen.body: 特定街区は、街区単位で高さや容積率、壁面の位置などを都市計画で個別に定める制度です。その代わりに、広場や歩道などの空地を確保することが求められるのが一般的です。東京の西新宿の超高層ビル群などでも使われてきた、歴史の長い仕組みです。

hojosen.title: 津田沼の駅前競争
hojosen.body: 津田沼駅の周辺は、かつて大型の商業施設が集まり、激しく客を取り合ったことで知られます。百貨店や専門店の撤退が進んだ後、南口でも再開発の計画が動いており、駅の両側で「商業の街」から「住む街」への組み替えが進んでいます。

en.title: Two cities near Tokyo draft rules for a 160 m tower on the former Tsudanuma PARCO site
en.summary: Narashino and Funabashi, two cities in Chiba Prefecture east of Tokyo, have drafted a city plan for the former PARCO department store site at Tsudanuma Station. It splits the site into two blocks with height limits of 40 m (130 ft) and 160 m (525 ft), and aims for a final decision in fiscal 2027.
body: Narashino and Funabashi, neighboring cities in Chiba Prefecture east of Tokyo, have drawn up a draft city plan for redeveloping the site of the former Tsudanuma PARCO, a shopping complex at the north exit of JR Tsudanuma Station. The draft divides the land into two blocks and caps building heights at 40 m (130 ft) for Block A and 160 m (525 ft) for Block B.

According to reports, Block A, on the site of the former PARCO Building A, would get a six-story commercial and office building. Block B would get a tower of about 40 stories, with shops on the lower floors and condominiums above. Because the land straddles the border between the two cities, they will run the city planning procedures together and aim to finalize the plan during fiscal 2027 (April 2027 to March 2028).

Since PARCO closed, Mitsui Fudosan Residential opened ATOCHI, a plaza in front of the station, on the former Building A site on October 1 as a temporary use until full-scale development begins. The draft is the first time the future of the site has been set out in numbers.
en.commentary: It looks like the south and north sides of the station will end up with towers of about the same height facing each other. The upper limit for Block B on the north side is 160 m. That's almost the same height as Tsudanuma The Tower, the high-rise condominium on the south side. The system being used here, the special urban block, is a bit unusual. Normally, the size of a building is capped by the floor area ratio (FAR) set for each zoning district, meaning the limit on how much floor space you can stack up relative to the size of the lot. In a special urban block, the city plan sets rules just for that block, fixing its height and floor area one by one. In clothing terms, it's less like picking from a ready-to-wear size chart and more like a made-to-measure suit, right? Here, Block A is kept low and Block B goes high. The plan draws a clear line between the low-rise side and the side where the tower stands. One more unusual point is that the site straddles the border between Funabashi and Narashino. Two cities deciding the same city plan at the same time, for one building. The target for the decision is fiscal 2027.
briefing: According to reports, the two cities' schedule assumes construction of the Block A building could start as early as fiscal 2028, with completion in fiscal 2031. A start date for Block B was not given in what we could confirm.

Block B's 160 m (525 ft) height is reported to be almost the same as Tsudanuma The Tower, a high-rise condominium at the station's south exit. Towers of similar height would face each other across the station.
ATOCHI, the plaza on the former Building A site, opened on October 1, 2026, as a project by Mitsui Fudosan Residential to make temporary use of the land until future development.

hojosen.title: What a special urban block is
hojosen.body: A special urban block is a Japanese city planning tool that sets height, floor area ratio, wall positions and similar rules individually for a single block. In return, the developer is generally required to provide open space such as plazas and sidewalks. It is a long-standing system that has also been used for places like the skyscraper district of West Shinjuku in Tokyo.

hojosen.title: Tsudanuma's retail battles
hojosen.body: The area around Tsudanuma Station was once known for its many large shopping complexes competing hard for customers. After department stores and specialty stores pulled out, redevelopment plans have also moved forward on the south side, and both sides of the station are shifting from a shopping district to a place to live.

stories.title: 亀戸駅北口で約1.8haの再開発へ 地権者が準備組合を設立、NTT都市開発が事業協力
stories.summary: JR亀戸駅の北側、明治通りと商店街に接する約1.8haで再開発の準備組合が発足。古い建物の密集や浸水のリスクといった課題の解消をめざします。
body: 東京都江東区のJR総武線・東武亀戸線の亀戸駅北口で、市街地再開発に向けた「亀戸五丁目地区市街地再開発準備組合」が設立されました。NTT都市開発が11月5日に発表したもので、設立は9月13日。準備組合は事業協力者として同社を選んでいます。
検討しているのは、駅の北側で明治通りと亀戸中央通り商店街に接する、亀戸五丁目内の約1.8ヘクタールです。この地区には、古い建物が密集し、道が狭く、水害時に浸水するおそれがあるといった防災上の課題があるとされています。区域は今後の協議で変わる可能性があります。
今後は準備組合とNTT都市開発が中心になり、土地や建物の権利を持つ人たちの意向を確かめて合意をつくりながら、都市計画や建物の計画、事業計画を検討します。建物の規模や完成時期は、まだ示されていません。
stories.commentary: 駅前の古い店も住まいも、一度たたんで大きな一つの建物に引っ越す。市街地再開発は、ざっくり言えばそういう仕組みなんです。土地や建物の権利を、完成後の新しいビルの床と交換します。だから地区の全員の暮らしと商売に関わる。亀戸五丁目では、地権者108者のうち約6割が準備組合の設立に賛同しました。法律上、本格的な組合をつくるには、土地の所有者などのそれぞれ3分の2以上の同意が必要になります。今回の地区が抱える課題の一つは、浸水のリスクです。江東区は低い土地が広がるエリアで、道が狭く古い建物が並ぶ街区は、水が出たときに逃げにくく、助けにも入りにくい。建て替えで解決できることは多いと思います。一方で、亀戸中央通り商店街に面した、通りに店が並ぶにぎわいも、この街の財産です。防災のための大きな建物と、商店街の路面のにぎわい。その両方をどこまで残せるんでしょうね。
briefing: 地権者たちは2023年11月から勉強会を重ね、2024年12月には有志の地権者が「亀戸北口まちづくり発起人会」を組織しました。準備組合の設立にあたっては、地権者108者のうち約6割から賛同を得たとされています。
準備組合は、正式な再開発組合の前段階にあたる任意の組織です。今後、都市計画の決定や組合の設立認可などの手続きを経て、事業が本格的に動き出します。
発表はNTT都市開発（NTTアーバンソリューションズグループ）によるもので、事業協力者は、計画づくりや権利者との調整などで準備組合を支える役割を担います。

hojosen.title: 低い土地と防災
hojosen.body: 江東区を含む東京の東部には、地面の高さが満潮時の海面より低い、いわゆる海抜ゼロメートル地帯が広がっています。大きな水害への備えとして、建物を高くしたり、上の階に避難できる場所を設けたりする再開発は、この地域で防災の手段と位置づけられてきました。

hojosen.title: 準備組合から完成まで
hojosen.body: 市街地再開発は、準備組合の発足から都市計画の決定、組合の設立、権利の変換、着工、完成まで、10年を超えることも珍しくありません。初期の段階では、区域や建物の規模が協議の中で変わっていくのが一般的です。

en.title: Landowners at Tokyo's Kameido Station launch a 1.8-hectare redevelopment group with NTT Urban Development
en.summary: A redevelopment preparation association has formed on about 1.8 hectares (4.4 acres) north of JR Kameido Station in eastern Tokyo, next to Meiji-dori avenue and a shopping street. It aims to address crowded old buildings and flood risk.
body: A preparation association for an urban redevelopment project, a Japanese scheme in which landowners pool their plots to build a larger complex, has been set up at the north exit of Kameido Station in Tokyo's Koto Ward, served by the JR Sobu Line and the Tobu Kameido Line. NTT Urban Development announced on November 5 that the Kameido 5-chome District Urban Redevelopment Preparation Association was formed on September 13 and has chosen the company as its project partner.

The area under study is about 1.8 hectares (4.4 acres) in Kameido 5-chome, north of the station and bordering Meiji-dori avenue and the Kameido Chuo-dori shopping street. The district is said to face disaster-prevention problems, including densely packed old buildings, narrow streets and a risk of flooding. The boundaries may change through future discussions.

Going forward, the association and NTT Urban Development will take the lead in confirming the wishes of people who hold rights to land and buildings and building agreement among them, while working on the city plan, the building plan and the project plan. The size of the buildings and the completion date have not yet been announced.
en.commentary: The old shops and homes in front of the station all close up once and move into one big building. Put simply, that's how an urban redevelopment project works. Rights to land and buildings are exchanged for floor space in the new building once it's done. So it touches the life and business of everyone in the district. In Kameido 5-chome, about 60% of the 108 landowners backed setting up the preparation association. Under the law, forming a full redevelopment association requires the consent of at least two-thirds of each group, such as landowners. One of the problems this district faces is flood risk. Koto Ward is an area of low-lying land, and blocks with narrow streets lined with old buildings are hard to escape from when water rises, and hard for rescuers to get into. I think rebuilding can solve a lot of that. On the other hand, the bustle of shops lining the street along the Kameido Chuo-dori shopping street is also one of this neighborhood's assets. Big buildings for disaster prevention, and the street-level life of a shopping street. How much of both can be kept, I wonder?
briefing: The landowners have held study sessions since November 2023, and in December 2024 a group of volunteer landowners formed the Kameido North Exit Community Development Founders' Group. About 60% of the 108 landowners are said to have supported setting up the preparation association.

A preparation association is a voluntary body that comes before a formal redevelopment association. The project will get fully underway after procedures such as a city planning decision and approval to form the association.

The announcement came from NTT Urban Development (part of the NTT Urban Solutions group). A project partner supports the preparation association with tasks such as drawing up plans and coordinating with rights holders.

hojosen.title: Low ground and disaster risk
hojosen.body: Eastern Tokyo, including Koto Ward, has wide areas of so-called zero-meter land, where the ground is lower than sea level at high tide. Redevelopments that raise buildings or add places where people can take refuge on upper floors have been treated as a disaster-prevention measure in this area.

hojosen.title: From association to completion
hojosen.body: An urban redevelopment project often takes more than 10 years, from forming a preparation association through the city planning decision, setting up the association, converting rights, starting construction and completion. In the early stages, it is common for the boundaries and building size to change through discussions.

stories.title: 続報：中古住宅の「手入れ」を値段に映す仕組みへ 国交省が維持保全の評価を話し合うWGを設置
stories.summary: 国交省が11月5日、住宅の点検や修繕の積み重ねをどう評価するかを議論するワーキンググループの開催を発表。中古住宅の値付けの見直しにつなげます。
body: 国土交通省は11月5日、「住宅の維持保全状況に係る評価及び既存住宅の性能評価に関する検討ワーキンググループ」の第1回会合を開くと発表しました。住み手がどれだけきちんと点検や修繕をしてきたかを評価する方法と、すでに建っている住宅の性能をどう評価するかを話し合います。
10月11日号でお伝えした「住宅の維持保全・流通に関する制度検討会」の下に置かれる作業部会の一つです。検討会の下には、住宅の履歴情報や、欠陥への備え・消費者保護を扱うワーキンググループも設けられ、履歴情報のグループは10月28日に初会合を開いています。
日本経済新聞によると、国交省は定期点検や修繕が適切に行われた住宅について、火災保険やローンの契約などで優遇を受けられるようにすることを検討しています。手入れの履歴を、売買の際に買い手や金融機関が確認できる仕組みも想定しているといいます。
stories.commentary: 築25年の木造住宅は、どれだけ大事に住んでも建物の値段がほぼゼロ。日本の中古住宅の売買では、長くそんな見方が続いてきました。屋根を塗り直しても、外壁のひびを早めに埋めても、査定の紙の上では築年数に負けてしまうんです。車で言えば、毎年きちんと点検に出してきた車と、一度も見せていない車が同じ値段で引き取られるようなものですよね。今回のワーキンググループが扱うのは、その「手入れ」をどう数字にするかです。ポイントは記録だと思うんです。いつ、どこを、誰が直したのか。それが残っていなければ、どれだけ手をかけても買い手からは見えません。逆に言えば、評価の物差しが決まれば、家を直す理由がひとつ増えます。点検の記録は、誰が、どこに、何年残しておくべきなんでしょうね。
briefing: 親の検討会である「住宅の維持保全・流通に関する制度検討会」は10月に初会合を開き、2027年3月に最終的な提言をまとめる方針と報じられています。提言は法制度や施策への反映をめざすとされています。
検討会の下には、今回の「維持保全評価・既存評価」と「履歴情報」に加え、「瑕疵担保履行制度・消費者保護」の三つのワーキンググループが置かれています。瑕疵担保履行制度は、新築住宅の欠陥を補修する費用を保険や供託で確保させる仕組みです。
国交省は2014年にも、中古戸建て住宅の建物評価を改善するための指針をまとめています。建物を基礎・躯体と内外装・設備に分けて評価し、基礎・躯体は適切に維持管理されていれば少なくとも50〜60年程度の価値があると考える内容でした。

sources.name: ハウジング・トリビューン

hojosen.title: 築20年でゼロの慣行
hojosen.body: 日本の中古住宅の取引では、個々の住宅の状態にかかわらず、木造戸建ての建物価値を築20〜25年ほどでゼロとみなす慣行が続いてきました。2014年の国の指針はこれを改めようとしたものですが、市場への定着は道半ばとされています。今回の議論は、評価の物差しに「手入れの実績」を加えようとする点で、その延長線上にあります。

hojosen.title: 新築高騰が後押し
hojosen.body: 首都圏の新築マンションの平均価格が1億円を超えるなど、新築住宅の価格は上がり続けています。新築に手が届きにくくなるなか、すでにある住宅をきちんと評価して流通させることは、住まいの選択肢を広げる手段として注目されています。

en.title: Update: Japan moves to let upkeep raise the value of used homes, as MLIT sets up a working group on maintenance records
en.summary: On November 5, Japan's construction and housing ministry announced the first meeting of a working group that will discuss how to evaluate the inspections and repairs owners put into their homes, with an eye to changing how used homes are priced.
body: On November 5, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT), which oversees building and housing policy in Japan, announced that it will hold the first meeting of a working group on evaluating how well homes have been maintained and on assessing the performance of existing homes. The group will discuss how to rate the inspections and repairs that owners have carried out, and how to evaluate the performance of homes that are already built.

The working group sits under the Study Group on Systems for the Maintenance and Circulation of Housing, which we reported on Oct 11. Other working groups under that study group cover housing history records and protection against defects and for consumers. The housing records group held its first meeting on October 28.

According to the Nikkei, Japan's main business daily, MLIT is considering letting homes that have received proper regular inspections and repairs qualify for better terms on things like fire insurance and mortgage contracts. It is also said to be looking at a system that would let buyers and lenders check a home's maintenance history when it is sold.
en.commentary: A wooden house that's 25 years old is worth almost nothing as a building, no matter how carefully it's been lived in. That's how used homes have long been viewed in Japanese real estate deals. You can repaint the roof or fill cracks in the outside walls early, and on the appraisal sheet the building's age still wins. In car terms, it's like a car that's been taken in for inspection every year being bought back for the same price as one that's never been checked, right? What this working group is tackling is how to turn that upkeep into numbers. I think the key is records. When was it fixed, where, and by whom? If that isn't written down, buyers can't see it, no matter how much care went in. Put the other way, once there's a yardstick for evaluating upkeep, owners get one more reason to fix their homes. Who should keep those inspection records, where, and for how many years, I wonder?
briefing: The parent study group, the Study Group on Systems for the Maintenance and Circulation of Housing, held its first meeting in October and is reported to plan its final recommendations for March 2027. The recommendations are meant to feed into laws and policy.

Under the study group are three working groups: this one on maintenance and existing-home evaluation, one on housing history records, and one on the defect warranty system and consumer protection. The defect warranty system requires builders to secure money, through insurance or deposits, to repair defects in new homes.

MLIT also drew up guidelines in 2014 to improve how the buildings of used detached houses are valued. They split a building into the foundation and structure on one side and the interior, exterior and equipment on the other, and treated the foundation and structure as keeping value for at least about 50 to 60 years if properly maintained.

hojosen.title: Zero value at 20 years
hojosen.body: In Japan's used-home market, the building on a wooden detached house has long been treated as worth zero after about 20 to 25 years, regardless of its actual condition. The government's 2014 guidelines tried to change that, but they are said to be only partly established in the market. The current discussion extends that effort by adding a home's record of upkeep to the yardstick.

hojosen.title: Pushed by new-home prices
hojosen.body: Prices of new homes keep rising, with the average price of a new condominium in the Tokyo area topping ¥100 million. As new homes slip out of reach, properly valuing and selling existing homes is drawing attention as a way to widen people's housing options.

namesEn.国土交通省（公式）: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (official)

stories.title: 「空飛ぶクルマ」の離着陸場、愛知県が初の整備計画 県営名古屋空港で28年度内に供用へ
stories.summary: 愛知県が11月2日、県営名古屋空港に「空飛ぶクルマ」専用の離着陸場を整える基本計画を公表しました。既存の施設を格納庫に使い、2028年度内の供用をめざします。
body: 愛知県は11月2日、県営名古屋空港（愛知県豊山町）に、電動で垂直に離着陸する「空飛ぶクルマ」の離着陸場を整備する基本計画を公表しました。県内で初めての専用の離着陸場になります。同日に開いた県のプロジェクト会合で報告しました。
計画では、空港内にある既存の県飛行研究センターを機体の格納庫として活用し、機体を止める駐機エリアを2カ所設けます。充電器は運航する事業者が設置します。2027年3月までに実施設計を終え、27年度に受変電設備などの工事に入り、28年度内の供用開始を予定しています。
完成後は、民間事業者によるデモ飛行や遊覧飛行に使ってもらう想定で、将来の商用運航もにらみます。ただし、実際に使えるようになる時期は、機体の開発や国の安全認証の取得の進み具合にも左右されるとしています。
stories.commentary: 新しい滑走路も、大きなターミナルビルも建てません。今回の計画の中心は、すでにある建物の使い回しなんです。空港内の県の研究施設を格納庫にして、機体を止める場所を2カ所つくる。充電器は運航会社が持ち込む。新しく建てるものを最小限に抑えた計画です。空飛ぶクルマの離着陸場は、地上で言えばバス停と車庫と給油所をひとまとめにしたような施設です。滑走路がいらないぶん、思ったよりコンパクトじゃないですか。ただ、機体がいつ飛べるようになるかは、まだ国の認証しだい。だから先に大きな建物をつくらず、既存の空港と施設で始める判断は理にかなっていると思います。駅前やビルの屋上に乗り場が並ぶのは、その先の話です。供用開始の目標は、2028年度内です。
briefing: 経済産業省と国土交通省は2026年3月に「空の移動革命に向けたロードマップ」を改訂し、空飛ぶクルマの商用運航の開始時期を2027年から2028年と明記しました。愛知県の計画は、この国の目標時期に合わせた形です。
愛知県は2026年1月の時点で、県営名古屋空港を社会実装を先導する拠点と位置づけ、2028年度をめどに充電設備などを整える方針を示していました。今回の計画で、その中身とスケジュールが具体的になりました。
県の過去の調査では、遊覧飛行や二地点間の移動の拠点候補として、愛・地球博記念公園、名古屋城、名古屋港の各エリアも挙げられています。

hojosen.title: 大阪では補助金で
hojosen.body: 大阪府は、空飛ぶクルマの専用離着陸場などの拠点を整える民間事業者に補助金を出す制度を設けています。愛知県が県の施設を使って自ら整備するのに対し、大阪は民間の整備を後押しする形で、拠点づくりの進め方は自治体によって分かれています。

hojosen.title: 既存の空港から始める
hojosen.body: 空飛ぶクルマは、機体の安全認証や運航のルールづくりが進行中で、いつ・どれだけ飛ぶかの見通しがまだ固まっていません。そのため各地で、すでに管制や安全管理の仕組みがある空港を最初の拠点にする動きが目立ちます。

en.title: Aichi Prefecture unveils its first plan for a flying-car port, at Prefectural Nagoya Airport by fiscal 2028
en.summary: On November 2, Aichi Prefecture in central Japan released a basic plan for a dedicated takeoff and landing site for flying cars at Prefectural Nagoya Airport. It will reuse an existing building as a hangar and aims to open within fiscal 2028.
body: On November 2, Aichi Prefecture, whose capital is Nagoya, released a basic plan to build a takeoff and landing site for electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, known in Japan as flying cars, at Prefectural Nagoya Airport in the town of Toyoyama. It will be the prefecture's first dedicated site for them. The plan was reported at a prefectural project meeting held the same day.

Under the plan, an existing prefectural flight research center inside the airport will be used as a hangar for the aircraft, and two parking areas for aircraft will be built. Chargers will be installed by the companies that operate the flights. The prefecture plans to finish detailed design by March 2027, start work on power receiving and transforming equipment and other facilities in fiscal 2027, and open the site within fiscal 2028. Japan's fiscal year runs from April to March.

Once complete, the site is expected to be used by private companies for demonstration flights and sightseeing flights, with commercial service as a future goal. The prefecture notes, however, that when the site can actually be used will also depend on progress in developing the aircraft and in obtaining national safety certification.
en.commentary: No new runway, and no big terminal building either. The heart of this plan is reusing a building that already exists. A prefectural research facility inside the airport becomes the hangar, and two spots are made for parking aircraft. The operators bring their own chargers. It's a plan that keeps new construction to a minimum. On the ground, a flying-car port is like a bus stop, a garage and a gas station rolled into one. Since there's no runway, it's more compact than you might think, isn't it? But when the aircraft will actually be able to fly still depends on national certification. So I think the decision not to build anything big first, and to start with an existing airport and facility, makes sense. Rows of boarding points in front of train stations and on building rooftops come later. The target for opening is within fiscal 2028.
briefing: In March 2026, Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism revised their roadmap for the air mobility revolution and stated that commercial flying-car service would start between 2027 and 2028. Aichi's plan is timed to match that national target.

As of January 2026, Aichi had already positioned Prefectural Nagoya Airport as a base to lead the real-world rollout and said it would install charging facilities and more around fiscal 2028. The new plan gives that idea concrete contents and a schedule.
Earlier prefectural studies also listed the areas around the Aichi Expo memorial park, Nagoya Castle and the Port of Nagoya as candidate bases for sightseeing flights and point-to-point travel.

hojosen.title: Subsidies in Osaka
hojosen.body: Osaka Prefecture runs a subsidy program for private companies that build bases such as dedicated flying-car takeoff and landing sites. While Aichi is building its own site using a prefectural facility, Osaka supports private construction, so local governments are taking different routes.

hojosen.title: Starting from airports
hojosen.body: Safety certification for flying cars and rules for operating them are still being worked out, so when and how much they will fly is not yet settled. That is why many places are choosing airports, which already have air traffic control and safety management in place, as their first bases.

stories.title: 米誌の「今年の建築」にブラジル・サンパウロのオフィス アルキペオ、浸水しやすい工場地帯に
stories.summary: 米建築誌アーキテクチュラル・レコードが、2026年の「ビルディング・オブ・ザ・イヤー」にサンパウロのオフィス複合施設「アルキペオ」を選びました。
body: 米国の建築専門誌「アーキテクチュラル・レコード」は、2026年の同誌の建築賞「レコード・アワード」の受賞作を発表し、最高賞にあたる「ビルディング・オブ・ザ・イヤー」に、ブラジル・サンパウロのオフィス複合施設「Arquipeo（アルキペオ）」を選びました。11月4日にニューヨークで表彰が行われました。
アルキペオは、ブラジルの設計事務所「エストゥジオ・グスタボ・ウトラボ」の設計です。まずオフィス・ワークプレイス部門で受賞し、その中から全体の最高賞にも選ばれました。
建物があるのは、浸水が起きやすい工業地帯のヴィラ・レオポルディナ地区です。5階建てで主にコンクリート造。外側を穴のあいた鋼板のスクリーンで包み、ずらして配置した柱の格子によって、通り道や中庭、テラスがつながる構成になっています。不動産会社ブルックフィールド・プロパティーズが開発し、2024年10月に開業しました。
stories.commentary: オフィスビルと聞いて思い浮かぶのは、ガラス張りの高い塔ではないでしょうか。アルキペオは逆で、5階建てと低く、横に大きく広がっています。柱の並びをわざとずらして、その隙間を通り道や中庭、テラスにしているんです。ビルの中を歩くというより、小さな街の路地を抜けていく感覚に近いのだと思います。もう一つ面白いのは場所です。浸水しやすい元工場地帯に建っています。日本でも、湾岸や川沿いの工場跡地がオフィスやマンションに変わる例は珍しくありません。水が出やすい土地で、地面に近い階をどう使うか。工場地帯の記憶を残しながら、新しい働く場所をどうつくるか。日本の再開発と同じ問いを、サンパウロの低いオフィスが先に解こうとしている。そういう時代なんだと思います。
briefing: 受賞作の表彰は、同誌が毎年開く「イノベーション・カンファレンス」に合わせてニューヨークで行われました。
アルキペオは、テナントの要望に合わせて建てる「ビルト・トゥ・スーツ」型の開発です。ブラジルのグリーンビルディング評議会は、ヴィラ・レオポルディナ地区の企業建築と、工業地帯から都市への移り変わりを象徴する建物として紹介しています。
設計者のグスタボ・ウトラボ氏は、ブラジル中部の寄宿学校「チルドレン・ビレッジ（アルデイア・インファンチウ）」で知られる建築家です。この学校は2018年に英国王立建築家協会（RIBA）の国際賞を受けています。

hojosen.title: 工場地帯の高密度化
hojosen.body: ヴィラ・レオポルディナ地区はもともと工場が集まっていた地域で、サンパウロ市が主導する都市開発事業のもと、建物の高層化と高密度化が進んでいます。アルキペオは、その流れのなかで低く広い建物を選んだ例です。

hojosen.title: ブラジル建築の系譜
hojosen.body: ブラジルは、オスカー・ニーマイヤーやパウロ・メンデス・ダ・ロシャらコンクリートを大胆に使う建築家を生んだ国です。アルキペオの主にコンクリートでつくる構成も、その土地の建築文化とつながっています。

en.title: Architectural Record names Sao Paulo office complex Arquipeo its 2026 Building of the Year
en.summary: The US architecture magazine Architectural Record has chosen Arquipeo, an office complex in Sao Paulo, Brazil, as its 2026 Building of the Year. The building sits in a flood-prone industrial district.
body: The US architecture magazine Architectural Record announced the winners of its 2026 Record Awards and gave its top honor, Building of the Year, to Arquipeo, an office complex in Sao Paulo, Brazil. The winners were honored in New York on November 4.
Arquipeo was designed by the Brazilian firm Estudio Gustavo Utrabo. It first won the Office and Workplace category and was then picked from among the category winners as the overall top building.

The building stands in Vila Leopoldina, a flood-prone industrial district. It is five stories tall and mainly concrete. It is wrapped in a screen of perforated steel, and a staggered grid of columns creates connected pathways, courtyards and terraces. It was developed by Brookfield Properties and opened in October 2024.
en.commentary: When you think of an office building, you probably picture a tall glass tower, don't you? Arquipeo is the opposite. It's only five stories and spreads out wide. The column grid is deliberately staggered, and the gaps become pathways, courtyards and terraces. I think it feels less like walking through a building and more like cutting through the alleys of a small town. The other interesting thing is the location. It stands in a former factory district that floods easily. In Japan, too, it's not unusual for old factory sites along the bay or rivers to turn into offices and condominiums. On land prone to flooding, how do you use the floors closest to the ground? How do you create a new place to work while keeping the memory of an industrial area? A low office building in Sao Paulo is trying to answer the same questions Japan's redevelopment faces, ahead of us. I think that's the kind of era we're in.
briefing: The winners were honored in New York alongside the magazine's annual Innovation Conference.

Arquipeo is a built-to-suit development, meaning it was built to a tenant's requirements. The Green Building Council Brasil describes it as a building that symbolizes corporate architecture in Vila Leopoldina and the district's shift from an industrial area to an urban one.

The architect, Gustavo Utrabo, is known for the Children Village (Aldeia Infantil), a boarding school in central Brazil. The school received the RIBA International Prize from the Royal Institute of British Architects in 2018.

hojosen.title: Densifying a factory district
hojosen.body: Vila Leopoldina was originally a district full of factories, and under an urban development program led by the City of Sao Paulo, its buildings are getting taller and denser. Arquipeo is an example of choosing a low, wide building within that trend.

hojosen.title: A Brazilian lineage
hojosen.body: Brazil produced architects such as Oscar Niemeyer and Paulo Mendes da Rocha, who used concrete boldly. Arquipeo's mainly concrete construction connects to that local building culture.

stories.title: 川崎市の担当部長を官製談合の疑いで逮捕 塗装・防水工事の非公表価格を業界団体に漏らしたか
stories.summary: 川崎市発注の塗装・防水工事の入札で、非公表の工事価格を業界団体側に漏らした疑いで、神奈川県警が11月4日に市の担当部長を逮捕しました。
body: 神奈川県警は11月4日、川崎市が発注した塗装・防水工事の入札をめぐり、非公表の「工事価格」を業者側に漏らしたとして、市まちづくり局の担当部長（59）を官製談合防止法違反（入札妨害）などの疑いで逮捕しました。県警は認否を明らかにしていません。
逮捕容疑は、2024年ごろに行われた市内2施設の工事の一般競争入札で、業界団体「川崎塗装業協会」の事務局長に工事価格を伝え、共謀して協会に加盟する2社に落札させた疑いです。部長は当時、同局の施設整備部長でした。事務局長は市の元幹部で、県警は、事務局長が聞き出した工事価格をもとに最低制限価格を割り出し、業者側に伝わっていたとみています。
県警は協会の事務所や川崎市役所を家宅捜索しました。市のOBも関わって同じような不正が繰り返されていた疑いがあるとみて、関係者から話を聴くなどして実態の解明を進めています。
stories.commentary: 最低制限価格は、公共工事の入札にある「これより安いと失格」というラインです。安すぎる値段で落札されると、手抜きや下請けへのしわ寄せが起きやすい。それを防ぐための仕組みなんです。ただ、このラインは発注者が見積もった工事価格をもとに計算されます。だから工事価格さえ分かれば、ラインのぎりぎり上に札を入れられる。テストの合格点を前もって知っているようなもので、くじ引きに近い競争が、そうではなくなってしまいます。皆さんが払っている税金で建てる施設の値段が、こうして決まっていたとしたら、穏やかではいられないですよね。今回、疑いの中心にいるのは市の元幹部が事務局長を務める業界団体でした。発注する側と受ける側に、元同僚どうしのつながりが残っている。これは川崎だけの話ではなく、全国の自治体が抱える構造だと思います。容疑の段階なので、事実関係はこれからの捜査を待つ必要があります。価格を守る仕組みと人のつながりをどう切り分けるか、各地の発注者も問われていると思います。
briefing: 報道によると、対象になったのは市内2施設の塗装・防水工事で、いずれも一般競争入札でした。工事価格は、市が単価をもとに積算した見積額で、入札前には公表されていません。
事務局長は2009年に市を定年退職した元幹部と報じられています。県警は、協会内で落札する業者を決める仕切り役がいたとみています。
同じ11月4日には、静岡県発注の工事をめぐり逮捕された県職員と土木建設会社の役員ら3人を、静岡地検が官製談合防止法違反の罪などで起訴したことも報じられました。

hojosen.title: 価格を伏せる理由
hojosen.body: 多くの自治体では、予定価格や最低制限価格を事前に公表するかどうかを独自に決めています。事前に公表すると価格を探る働きかけは減る一方、公表額に札が集中してくじ引きになりやすいという指摘もあります。非公表にすれば、今度は価格を知る職員への働きかけが起きうるため、どちらにも弱点があります。

hojosen.title: 民間でも続く談合
hojosen.body: 10月にはマンション大規模修繕工事をめぐり、公正取引委員会が42社の談合を認定し、国交省が発注の適正化に向けた検討を始めています。公共・民間を問わず、発注者が価格を見極める力をどう持つかが、建設業界の共通の課題になっています。

en.title: Kawasaki city official arrested on suspicion of leaking confidential bid prices for painting and waterproofing work
en.summary: Kanagawa Prefectural Police arrested a senior official of Kawasaki, a city between Tokyo and Yokohama, on November 4 on suspicion of leaking undisclosed construction prices to an industry group ahead of bids for city painting and waterproofing jobs.
body: On November 4, Kanagawa Prefectural Police arrested a senior manager (59) in the urban development bureau of Kawasaki, a large city between Tokyo and Yokohama, on suspicion of violating the Act on Elimination and Prevention of Involvement in Bid Rigging (obstruction of bidding), a law aimed at public officials who help rig public tenders. He is suspected of leaking the city's undisclosed "construction price" to contractors ahead of tenders for painting and waterproofing work ordered by the city. Police have not said whether he admits the allegations.

According to the allegations, around 2024, in open competitive tenders for work at two city facilities, he passed the construction prices to the secretary-general of the Kawasaki Painting Contractors Association, an industry group, and conspired so that two member companies would win the contracts. At the time, he was head of the bureau's facilities department. The secretary-general is a former senior city official. Police believe the secretary-general used the prices he obtained to work out the minimum acceptable bid, and that this figure was then passed on to the contractors.

Police searched the association's office and Kawasaki City Hall. Suspecting that similar wrongdoing, also involving former city employees, had been repeated, they are questioning people involved to establish the full picture.
en.commentary: The minimum acceptable bid is the line in a public tender that says, "bid below this and you're disqualified." If a job is won at a price that's too low, cutting corners and squeezing subcontractors become more likely. The system exists to prevent that. But that line is calculated from the construction price the client estimates. So if you know the construction price, you can put in a bid just above the line. It's like knowing the passing score of a test in advance, and a competition that should be close to a lottery stops being one. If the price of a facility built with your tax money was being decided this way, you couldn't stay calm about it, right? In this case, at the center of the allegations is an industry group whose secretary-general is a former senior city official. Ties between former colleagues remain on both the side that orders work and the side that receives it. I think this is not just a Kawasaki problem but a structure that local governments across Japan share. These are still allegations, so the facts will have to wait for the investigation. How to separate the system that protects prices from personal connections is a question I think clients everywhere are being asked.
briefing: According to reports, the jobs in question were painting and waterproofing work at two city facilities, both put out to open competitive tender. The construction price is the city's estimate, calculated from unit costs, and is not made public before the tender.

The secretary-general is reported to be a former senior official who retired from the city at the mandatory age in 2009. Police believe someone in the association acted as a coordinator who decided which company would win.

Also on November 4, it was reported that the Shizuoka District Public Prosecutors Office had indicted three people, including a Shizuoka prefectural employee and an executive of a civil engineering company, who had been arrested over work ordered by the prefecture, on charges including violating the same anti-bid-rigging law.

hojosen.title: Why prices are kept secret
hojosen.body: Many local governments in Japan decide for themselves whether to publish the ceiling price or the minimum acceptable bid before a tender. Publishing them in advance reduces attempts to find out the price, but critics point out that bids then cluster at the published figure and the tender turns into a lottery. Keeping them secret means officials who know the price can become targets instead, so both approaches have weak points.

hojosen.title: Rigging in private work too
hojosen.body: In October, Japan's Fair Trade Commission found that 42 companies had rigged bids for large-scale repair work on condominiums, and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) began looking at ways to make ordering fairer. In both public and private work, how clients develop the ability to judge prices has become a shared challenge for the construction industry.

stories.title: ららぽーとTOKYO-BAY北館Ⅱ期が着工 中央広場を約3倍に広げ、28年夏に全面開業へ
stories.summary: 千葉・船橋の「ららぽーとTOKYO-BAY」で北館建て替えのⅡ期工事が始まりました。2028年夏の開業で、施設全体は約600店舗になります。
body: 三井不動産は11月4日、千葉県船橋市の「三井ショッピングパーク ららぽーとTOKYO-BAY」で進める北館の建て替え計画について、Ⅱ期エリアの建築工事に着手したと発表しました。開業は2028年夏の予定で、これで建て替えが完了し、施設が全面開業します。
ららぽーとTOKYO-BAYは1981年に開業した、ららぽーとの1号店です。北館の建て替えは2期に分けて進めており、Ⅰ期エリアは2025年10月に96店舗で開業しました。Ⅱ期エリアの店舗数は建て替え前の約150店舗から約200店舗に増え、施設全体では約600店舗の規模になる見込みです。
Ⅱ期では、これまでの中央広場を約3倍の広さに広げ、スポーツやエンターテインメントのイベントに使える屋内型の「スタジアムコート」を整備します。
stories.commentary: 45年。ららぽーとTOKYO-BAYが、1号店として船橋に開業してからの時間です。大型の商業施設を建て替えるとき、一番難しいのは「営業しながら」という条件なんです。全部閉めて一気に建て替えれば工事は楽ですが、その間お客さんもお店も離れてしまいます。だから敷地を区切って、半分ずつ建て替える。引っ越しで、住みながら部屋を一つずつ片づけていくのに似ています。Ⅰ期が開業して1年で、今度はⅡ期に取りかかる順番です。もう一つ注目したいのが、中央広場を約3倍にする「スタジアムコート」です。皆さんも、ネットで買い物が済む時代に、わざわざ足を運ぶ理由は、店の数より「そこで何が起きているか」に移ってきていると感じませんか。店舗面積を増やすだけでなく、人が集まって見る場所に面積を割いているのは、その表れだと思います。今度大きなショッピングモールに行ったら、吹き抜けや広場が建物のどこにあって、どれくらいの広さか見てみてください。
briefing: 北館全体の店舗面積は、建て替え前の約4万5000m2から約6万200m2に広がる計画です。
全面開業の具体的な日付はまだ示されておらず、「2028年夏」の予定とされています。

sources.name: 三井不動産（公式・PR TIMES）

hojosen.title: モールも建て替え期
hojosen.body: 1980年代から90年代に郊外で開業した大型商業施設は、建物や設備の更新時期を迎えています。閉館して解体するか、営業を続けながら段階的に建て替えるか、各地で判断が分かれています。

hojosen.title: 「体験」に面積を
hojosen.body: 近年の商業施設では、イベント広場や遊び場、スポーツ施設など、物を売らない場所の面積を広げる例が増えています。来館の動機をつくり、滞在時間を延ばす狙いがあります。

stories.sourceName: 三井不動産（公式・PR TIMES）

en.title: LaLaport TOKYO-BAY near Tokyo starts phase two of its north wing rebuild, with a full reopening set for summer 2028
en.summary: Construction has begun on the second phase of the north wing rebuild at LaLaport TOKYO-BAY, a shopping mall in Funabashi just east of Tokyo. It opens in summer 2028, bringing the whole mall to about 600 stores.
body: Mitsui Fudosan announced on November 4 that it has started construction on the phase two area of its north wing rebuild at Mitsui Shopping Park LaLaport TOKYO-BAY in Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture, a suburb just east of Tokyo. The opening is planned for summer 2028, which will complete the rebuild and mark the mall's full reopening.

LaLaport TOKYO-BAY opened in 1981 as the first LaLaport, now a large chain of shopping malls. The north wing is being rebuilt in two phases, and the phase one area opened with 96 stores in October 2025. The phase two area will grow from about 150 stores before the rebuild to about 200, bringing the whole mall to about 600 stores.
In phase two, the former central plaza will be expanded to about three times its size, creating an indoor "stadium court" that can host sports and entertainment events.
en.commentary: 45 years. That's how long it has been since LaLaport TOKYO-BAY opened in Funabashi as the chain's first mall. When you rebuild a big shopping mall, the hardest condition is doing it while staying open. Closing everything and rebuilding in one go makes construction easier, but in the meantime both shoppers and stores drift away. So you divide the site and rebuild it half at a time. It's like moving house while still living there, clearing one room at a time. Phase one opened a year ago, and now it's phase two's turn. The other thing I want to point out is the "stadium court" that makes the central plaza about three times bigger. Now that you can do your shopping online, don't you feel the reason to actually go somewhere has shifted from the number of stores to what's happening there? Rather than just adding store space, they're giving floor area to a place where people gather and watch. I think that's a sign of it. Next time you're at a big shopping mall, look at where the atriums and plazas are in the building and how big they are.
briefing: The north wing's total store area is planned to grow from about 45,000 m² (484,000 sq ft) before the rebuild to about 60,200 m² (648,000 sq ft).
No specific date has been given for the full reopening yet; it is planned for "summer 2028."

hojosen.title: Malls reach rebuilding age
hojosen.body: Many large suburban shopping centers that opened in Japan in the 1980s and 1990s have reached the point where their buildings and equipment need renewal. Across the country, owners are split between closing and demolishing, or rebuilding in stages while staying open.

hojosen.title: Space for experiences
hojosen.body: Recent shopping centers increasingly devote more floor area to places that don't sell anything, such as event plazas, play areas and sports facilities. The aim is to give people a reason to come and to make them stay longer.

namesEn.三井不動産（公式・PR TIMES）: Mitsui Fudosan (official, PR TIMES press release)

stories.title: 仙台市泉区役所の新庁舎が竣工 地下鉄泉中央駅と直結、民間が建てて市が買い取る方式
stories.summary: 仙台市泉区役所の建て替えで、地上6階・地下2階の新庁舎が完成し、11月2日に竣工式が開かれました。2027年1月に開庁する予定です。
body: 仙台市が進める泉区役所の建て替え事業で、新しい庁舎が完成し、11月2日に竣工式が開かれました。新庁舎は地上6階・地下2階建てで、地下鉄南北線の泉中央駅と直結します。開庁は2027年1月の予定です。
事業は三菱地所が担い、2024年12月に着工しました。民間の事業者が新庁舎を建て、完成後に市が買い取る方式を採っています。
今後は旧庁舎を解体し、その跡に駐車場や区民広場などを整備します。敷地の一部では民間施設の開発も計画されており、街区全体の完成は2029年度の予定です。
stories.commentary: 区役所に行く日は、たいてい用事が決まっています。住民票、転入の手続き、子どもの手当。皆さんも、手続きのためだけに雨の中を歩いた経験、ありませんか。だから駅から濡れずに行けることは、思っている以上に効くんです。泉区の新庁舎は、地下鉄の泉中央駅と直結します。今回の建て替えで面白いのは、民間が建てて、完成したものを市が買う方式を選んでいる点です。自治体が自分で設計者と施工者を別々に選ぶやり方だと、入札が不調になると何か月も遅れることがあります。民間に任せれば、設計から工事まで一つの流れで進められる。2024年12月の着工から、ほぼ予定どおりの完成でした。もちろん、市がどこまで中身に注文をつけられるかは、契約の書き方しだいです。旧庁舎を壊したあとには、区民広場が整備されます。街区がすべて完成するのは、2029年度です。
briefing: 三菱地所が2024年12月に出した着工時の発表では、竣工は2026年10月末を予定していました。報道によると、工事はほぼその予定どおりに完了しています。
開庁の時期について、報道では「1月中旬から使い始める」「1月末に開庁」と伝え方に幅があり、具体的な日付は市の発表を待つ必要があります。
旧庁舎の解体は、新庁舎の開庁後の2月から始まると報じられています。

hojosen.title: 庁舎入札の不調
hojosen.body: 建設費の高騰で、自治体の庁舎建設では入札の不調が相次いでいます。10月には那須塩原市が新庁舎で3度目の入札公告を出し、岸和田市は設計施工一括の発注が不調となって分離発注に切り替えました。発注の方式選びが、庁舎計画の成否を左右する場面が増えています。

hojosen.title: 庁舎を街の核に
hojosen.body: 静岡市が清水庁舎を民間の複合ビルに入居させる方針を示すなど、庁舎を単独の建物ではなく、民間の開発と組み合わせて街づくりの拠点にする動きが各地で広がっています。

en.title: Sendai's new Izumi Ward Office is completed, linked to a subway station and built by a developer for the city to buy
en.summary: In Sendai, the largest city in Japan's Tohoku region, the new six-story, two-basement Izumi Ward Office has been completed, with a ceremony held on November 2. It is scheduled to open in January 2027.
body: The new building for the Izumi Ward Office in Sendai, the largest city in the Tohoku region of northeastern Japan, has been completed, and a completion ceremony was held on November 2. A ward office is the local branch of city hall where residents handle everyday paperwork. The new building has six floors above ground and two basement levels, and connects directly to Izumi-Chuo Station on the Sendai Subway Namboku Line. It is scheduled to open in January 2027.
The project is run by Mitsubishi Estate, and construction began in December 2024. Under the arrangement, the private developer builds the new office and the city buys it once it is finished.

Next, the old building will be demolished, and parking and a public plaza for residents will be built in its place. Private development is also planned on part of the site, and the whole block is scheduled for completion in fiscal 2029.
en.commentary: When you go to a ward office, it's usually for something specific: a residence certificate, registering a move, a child allowance. Haven't you ever walked through the rain just to do some paperwork? That's why being able to get there from the station without getting wet matters more than you'd think. The new Izumi Ward Office connects directly to Izumi-Chuo subway station. What's interesting about this rebuild is that the city chose a method where a private company builds it and the city buys the finished building. When a local government picks the designer and the contractor separately, as it usually does, a failed tender can cause delays of months. Hand it to the private sector, and design through construction can move as one process. From the start of construction in December 2024, it was finished almost exactly on schedule. Of course, how much the city can dictate what goes inside depends on how the contract is written. Once the old office is torn down, a public plaza for residents will be built. The whole block will be finished in fiscal 2029.
briefing: When Mitsubishi Estate announced the start of construction in December 2024, completion was planned for the end of October 2026. According to reports, the work was finished almost exactly on that schedule.
Reports differ on the opening, with some saying the office will start being used in mid-January and others saying it opens at the end of January, so the exact date will need to come from the city.
Demolition of the old building is reported to begin in February, after the new office opens.

hojosen.title: Failed tenders for city halls
hojosen.body: With construction costs rising, failed tenders for local government office buildings have been piling up in Japan. In October, Nasushiobara issued a tender notice for its new city hall for the third time, and Kishiwada switched to ordering design and construction separately after its design-build tender failed. The choice of procurement method is increasingly deciding whether a government building project succeeds.

hojosen.title: Offices at the heart of towns
hojosen.body: Shizuoka City has proposed moving its Shimizu branch office into a private mixed-use building, and similar moves are spreading across Japan to combine government offices with private development so they serve as hubs for the town, rather than standing as separate buildings.

stories.title: 松本の古い建物19会場にアート 「マツモト建築芸術祭」第2期が開幕、浅間温泉も初参加
stories.summary: 長野県松本市の歴史ある建物を会場にした「マツモト建築芸術祭2026 ADVANCE」の第2期が11月3日に開幕。18組が19会場で展示します。
body: 長野県松本市で、市内の歴史ある建物を会場にアート作品を展示する「マツモト建築芸術祭2026 ADVANCE」の第2期が、11月3日に開幕しました。会期は12月13日までで、国内外の18組のアーティストが、市内18施設・19会場で19の展覧会を開きます。参加作家には、李禹煥さん、チームラボ、ジュリアン・オピーさんらが名を連ねています。
今回は会場を「城下町」「旧六九商店街」「浅間温泉」「西」の4エリアに広げ、浅間温泉が初めて加わりました。浅間温泉エリアでは、大正8（1919）年に建てられた私設図書館「松門文庫」、かつて芸妓が稽古をした旧浅間温泉芸苑組合、老舗旅館の大浴場を改修したブックホテル「松本本箱」、空き家になった旧土産物店の4施設が会場になります。
第2期は、まちを歩いて会場を巡る周遊型の形式で、建築と作品の関係に焦点を当てます。
stories.commentary: 大浴場だった場所に、本が並んでいます。浅間温泉の「松本本箱」は、老舗旅館のお風呂を改修したブックホテルです。今回の芸術祭は、こういう「もとは別の用途だった建物」を会場に選んでいるのが面白いところなんです。美術館の展示室は、作品だけに目が向くよう、わざと白くて何もない箱につくられています。でも芸妓さんの稽古場や土産物店は違います。床の板の色や天井の低さ、窓から入る光に、その建物が過ごしてきた時間が残っている。そこに作品を置くと、作品を見ているつもりで、いつの間にか建物のほうも見ているんですよね。空き家になった旧土産物店が会場に入っているのも大事な点です。人が入る理由ができれば、閉じていた建物の中をもう一度見てもらえます。大正8年に建った松門文庫も、会場の一つです。
briefing: 旧六九商店街エリアでは、atelier m4 今町スタジオ、旧油三洋裁店、旧高松屋商店の3施設が会場になります。かつての洋裁店や商店の建物が、そのまま展示空間として使われます。
これまでの回は中心市街地を軸に開かれてきましたが、今回は温泉街まで会場を広げました。開場時間や休みの日は会場ごとに異なるため、訪れる前に公式サイトで確認するよう呼びかけられています。
今年は2期構成で、第1期は松本市立博物館を舞台に、複数の映像作品を同じ空間に並べる形式でした。芸術祭は「東アジア文化都市2026松本」のメインプログラムの一つに位置づけられています。

sources.name: マツモト建築芸術祭（公式）

hojosen.title: 見る祭と使う祭
hojosen.body: 近年は京都モダン建築祭やイケフェス大阪のように、ふだん入れない建物を公開する「建築祭」が全国で増えています。マツモト建築芸術祭は、建物を公開するだけでなく、そこにアート作品を置いて見せる点が特徴です。建物そのものを見せる催しと、建物を舞台として使う催しの両方が広がっているといえます。

hojosen.title: 空き家に人を入れる
hojosen.body: 芸術祭の会場に空き店舗や空き家を使う取り組みは、各地の芸術祭で行われてきました。期間限定でも人が出入りすることで、建物の状態が確かめられ、その後の使い道を考えるきっかけにもなります。

stories.sourceName: マツモト建築芸術祭（公式）

en.title: Matsumoto Architecture Art Festival opens its second phase across 19 old buildings, now including a hot spring town
en.summary: The second phase of the Matsumoto Architecture Art Festival 2026 ADVANCE, which places art in historic buildings in Matsumoto, Nagano Prefecture, opened on November 3. Eighteen artists and groups are showing work at 19 venues.
body: The second phase of the Matsumoto Architecture Art Festival 2026 ADVANCE opened on November 3 in Matsumoto, a castle town in Nagano Prefecture in the mountains of central Japan. The festival shows artworks inside the city's historic buildings. Running until December 13, it brings together 18 artists and groups from Japan and abroad, who are presenting 19 exhibitions at 19 venues in 18 buildings across the city. Participants include Lee Ufan, teamLab and Julian Opie.

This time the festival has spread into four areas: the castle town, the former Rokku shopping street, Asama Onsen and the west of the city. Asama Onsen, a hot spring town on the edge of Matsumoto, is taking part for the first time. Its four venues are a private library built in 1919, the former hall where geisha once practiced their arts, Matsumoto Honbako, a book hotel created by converting the large communal bath of a long-established inn, and a former souvenir shop that had been sitting empty.
The second phase is a walking format in which visitors tour the venues around the city, with a focus on the relationship between the buildings and the works.
en.commentary: Where there used to be a big communal bath, there are now shelves of books. Matsumoto Honbako in Asama Onsen is a book hotel made by converting the bathhouse of a long-established inn. What makes this festival interesting is that it picks buildings like this, ones that were originally made for something else. A museum gallery is deliberately built as a plain white box, so your eyes go only to the art. But a geisha practice hall or a souvenir shop is different. The color of the floorboards, the low ceilings, the light coming through the windows all hold the time the building has lived through. Put a work of art in there, and while you think you're looking at the art, at some point you start looking at the building too, right? It also matters that the empty former souvenir shop is one of the venues. Once people have a reason to step inside, a building that had been shut gets seen again. The private library built in 1919 is one of the venues too.
briefing: In the former Rokku shopping street area, the venues are three buildings: atelier m4 Imamachi Studio, a former dressmaker's shop and a former store. Old shop buildings are being used as exhibition spaces just as they are.

Past editions centered on the downtown area, but this time the venues extend all the way to the hot spring town. Opening hours and closing days differ from venue to venue, so visitors are asked to check the official website before going.

This year the festival has two phases. The first phase, held at the Matsumoto City Museum, placed several video works together in the same space. The festival is one of the main programs of Culture City of East Asia 2026 Matsumoto, a yearly program in which Japan, China and South Korea each name a city to host cultural events.

hojosen.title: Festivals to see, festivals to use
hojosen.body: In recent years, architecture festivals that open up buildings normally closed to the public, such as the Kyoto Modern Architecture Festival and Ikefes Osaka (the Living Architecture Museum Festival Osaka), have been multiplying across Japan. The Matsumoto festival stands out because it doesn't just open the buildings; it places artworks inside them. Both kinds of events, those that show the buildings themselves and those that use buildings as a stage, are spreading.

hojosen.title: Bringing people into empty buildings
hojosen.body: Art festivals in many parts of Japan have used empty shops and vacant houses as venues. Even for a limited period, having people come and go lets the condition of a building be checked, and can prompt thinking about what to do with it next.

stories.title: 千代田区、再開発マンションに「5年間の転売禁止」を要請 個別の事業者へは初めて
stories.summary: 東京都千代田区が10月27日、再開発で建つ新築分譲マンションに引き渡し後5年間の転売禁止を設けるよう、三菱地所レジデンスなどに要請しました。
body: 東京都千代田区は10月27日、区内の再開発で計画されている新築分譲マンションについて、引き渡し後5年間は転売を禁止する特約を設けるよう、三菱地所レジデンスなどに要請しました。同じ名義で複数の住戸を買うことの禁止も求めています。投機目的の購入を抑え、価格の高騰を和らげる狙いです。
対象は、市街地再開発事業などで容積率の緩和や補助金を受けて建てられる分譲マンションに限られ、純粋な民間開発の物件は含みません。区は2025年7月に、大手デベロッパーの業界団体である不動産協会へ同様の要請をしていましたが、個別の事業者に求めるのは今回が初めてです。
stories.commentary: 5年。新築マンションを買ってから、売ってはいけない期間として区が求めた長さです。民間どうしの売買に、なぜ区が口を出すのか。カギは「再開発」という条件にあります。再開発では、広場や歩道をつくってまちに貢献する代わりに、建物をふつうより大きく建ててよいことがあるんです。敷地の広さに対して、どれだけの床を積み上げてよいかという上限、つまり容積率を引き上げる仕組みです。補助金という税金が入ることもあります。まちのために特別に認めた床が、すぐ転売されて値上がりの材料になる。区が対象を再開発の物件に絞ったのは、そこを問題にしているからだと読めます。一方で、転勤や家族の事情で数年のうちに手放したい人もいるはずですよね。公共の手が入った住まいは、誰のためのものなんでしょうね。
briefing: 区が2025年7月に不動産協会へ要請した後、協会側は投機的な購入への対策を打ち出していました。今回の個別要請は、業界団体への呼びかけから一歩踏み込んだ形です。
要請は法律による規制ではなく、売買契約に特約を入れるよう事業者に求めるものです。純粋な民間開発のマンションは対象に含まれていません。

hojosen.title: 容積率の緩和
hojosen.body: 再開発では、公開空地や道路の整備など公共への貢献と引き換えに、通常より大きな容積率が認められることがあります。都心の超高層マンションの多くは、こうした仕組みで生まれた床でできています。その床の使われ方に自治体が条件をつけようとしているのが今回の要請です。

hojosen.title: 1億円を超えた平均
hojosen.body: 首都圏の新築マンションは、2026年4〜9月の平均価格が初めて1億円を超え、1億1494万円になりました（10月21日号でお伝えしました）。価格の高騰に投資目的の購入が影響しているとの見方があり、自治体が対策に乗り出す背景になっています。

en.title: Tokyo's Chiyoda Ward asks developers to ban resale of redevelopment condos for five years
en.summary: On October 27, Chiyoda Ward in central Tokyo asked Mitsubishi Estate Residence and other developers to add a clause banning resale for five years after handover to new condominiums planned in its redevelopment projects. It is the first time the ward has made such a request to individual companies.
body: Chiyoda Ward, the district at the heart of Tokyo that includes the Imperial Palace and the Marunouchi business area, on October 27 asked Mitsubishi Estate Residence and other developers to include a special clause banning resale for five years after handover in the contracts for new condominiums planned in the ward's redevelopment projects. It also asked them to ban buyers from purchasing multiple units under the same name. The aim is to curb speculative buying and ease soaring prices.

The request covers only condominiums built through urban redevelopment projects and similar schemes that receive a floor-area bonus or subsidies. Purely private developments are not included. In July 2025, the ward made a similar request to the Real Estate Companies Association of Japan, the industry group for major developers, but this is the first time it has made the request to individual companies.
en.commentary: Five years. That is how long the ward wants buyers of new condos to wait before they can sell. Why would a ward get involved in a sale between private parties? The key is the condition that these are redevelopment projects. In a redevelopment, a building is sometimes allowed to be bigger than usual in exchange for contributing to the city, for example by creating a plaza or a sidewalk. It works by raising the floor area ratio, the cap on how much floor space you can stack up relative to the size of the site. Subsidies, which means tax money, can also be involved. So floor space that was specially allowed for the good of the city gets resold right away and becomes fuel for rising prices. The ward limiting the request to redevelopment properties suggests that this is what it sees as the problem. On the other hand, there must be people who need to sell within a few years because of a job transfer or family circumstances, right? A home that public measures helped build: who is it really for?
briefing: After the ward's request to the Real Estate Companies Association of Japan in July 2025, the association came up with measures against speculative purchases. This new request to individual companies goes a step further than a call to an industry group.
The request is not a legal regulation. It asks developers to put a special clause in their sales contracts. Condominiums from purely private developments are not covered.

hojosen.title: The floor-area bonus
hojosen.body: In a redevelopment, a larger floor area ratio than usual is sometimes allowed in exchange for contributions to the public, such as open public space or new roads. Many of the high-rise condominiums in central Tokyo are made of floor space created this way. This request is the local government trying to attach conditions to how that floor space is used.

hojosen.title: An average above ¥100 million
hojosen.body: The average price of a new condominium in the Tokyo metropolitan area topped ¥100 million for the first time in April to September 2026, reaching ¥114.94 million, as we reported on Oct 21. Some see investment purchases as a factor behind the price surge, and that is part of why local governments are stepping in.

stories.title: 防災庁が11月2日に発足 初代担当相が「最低3日、できれば1週間分」の備蓄を緊急要請
stories.summary: 災害対応の司令塔となる防災庁が11月2日に発足。初代担当相の細野豪志氏は、水や食料を最低3日分、できれば1週間分備えるよう国民に要請しました。
body: 災害対応の司令塔となる「防災庁」が11月2日に発足しました。首相をトップとし、細野豪志氏が初代の担当相を務めます。省庁を横断して防災・災害対応を取りまとめる組織で、各省庁への勧告権も持ちます。
細野担当相は発足初日に「緊急要請」を出し、国民に水や食料、携帯トイレを最低3日分、できれば1週間分備蓄するよう呼びかけました。あわせて自治体や各省庁にも防災対策の強化を求め、年内をめどに対応の状況を確認するとしています。
stories.commentary: 最低3日、できれば1週間。この備蓄の呼びかけは、実は「家にいられること」が前提なんです。避難所に行かずに自宅で過ごす在宅避難は、建物が無事で、中が安全であって初めて成り立ちます。水は1人1日3リットルが目安とされています。4人家族で1週間なら84リットル、2リットルのペットボトルで42本です。これをどこに置くかは、立派な住まいの設計の問題なんですよね。もう一つは家具です。揺れで倒れた本棚が廊下をふさぐと、建物が無事でも外に出られなくなります。備蓄は、家の耐震と家具の置き方とセットで考える話だと思うんです。今度水を買い足すときは、玄関や廊下ではなく、崩れても通り道をふさがない場所に置いてみてください。
briefing: 発足日の11月2日は、政府が閣議決定で定めました。細野氏は復興相も務めています。
細野氏は発足前の10月13日の記者会見で、11月2日の発足時に各省庁へ要請を出す考えを示し、勧告権は要請が十分に実現されない場合の次の段階の手段だと説明していました。
備蓄の対象として挙げられた携帯トイレは、断水で水洗トイレが使えなくなったときのためのものです。水や食料と並べて呼びかけられた点が、今回の要請の特徴です。

hojosen.title: 在宅避難と耐震
hojosen.body: 大きな地震のあと、避難所の混雑や生活環境の問題から、自宅が安全なら自宅で過ごす「在宅避難」が勧められるようになっています。その前提になるのが建物の耐震性で、1981年に導入された新耐震基準が一つの目安とされます。備蓄の呼びかけは、住まいの安全性と切り離せません。

hojosen.title: 調整役から司令塔へ
hojosen.body: これまで国の防災は、内閣府の防災担当が各省庁の調整役を担ってきました。防災庁は首相をトップに置き、勧告権を持つことで、より強い司令塔を目指します。熊本地震からの復旧が続くなかでの発足になりました。

en.title: Japan launches its new Disaster Management Agency, and its first minister urges households to stock up
en.summary: Japan's Disaster Management Agency, the new command center for disaster response, launched on November 2. Its first minister, Goshi Hosono, asked the public to stock at least three days', and ideally a week's, worth of water and food.
body: Japan's Disaster Management Agency, set up to act as the country's command center for disaster response, launched on November 2. It is headed by the prime minister, and Goshi Hosono serves as its first minister. The agency coordinates disaster prevention and response across government ministries and has the power to issue recommendations to them.

On the agency's first day, Hosono issued an emergency request asking the public to stockpile water, food and portable toilets for at least three days, and ideally for a week. He also asked local governments and ministries to strengthen their disaster measures, and said the government would check on their progress by the end of the year.
en.commentary: At least three days, ideally a week. Here's the thing: this call to stock up assumes that you can stay in your home. Sheltering at home instead of going to an evacuation center only works if the building survives and it's safe inside. The usual guideline for water is 3 liters per person per day. For a family of four for a week, that's 84 liters, or 42 two-liter bottles. Where you put all that is a real question of home design, isn't it? The other issue is furniture. If a bookcase falls in the shaking and blocks the hallway, you can't get out even if the building is fine. I think stockpiling is something to think about together with your home's earthquake resistance and how your furniture is arranged. Next time you buy more water, try storing it somewhere other than the entryway or the hallway, where it won't block your way out even if it topples.
briefing: The launch date of November 2 was set by a Cabinet decision. Hosono also serves as Minister for Reconstruction, the post that oversees recovery from major disasters.

At a press conference on October 13, before the launch, Hosono said he intended to issue requests to the ministries when the agency launched on November 2. He explained that the power to issue recommendations is the next step to use if requests are not fully carried out.
The portable toilets on the list are for when water outages make flush toilets unusable. Listing them alongside water and food is a distinctive feature of this request.

hojosen.title: Sheltering at home and seismic safety
hojosen.body: After major earthquakes, sheltering at home if it is safe has come to be recommended, because evacuation centers get crowded and living conditions there are hard. That depends on the building's earthquake resistance, and the 1981 seismic code, the line that separates older and newer buildings in Japan, is one benchmark. A call to stockpile can't be separated from how safe your home is.

hojosen.title: From coordinator to command center
hojosen.body: Until now, the disaster management office of the Cabinet Office coordinated the national government's disaster work across ministries. The new agency, with the prime minister at its head and the power to issue recommendations, aims to be a stronger command center. It launched while recovery from this year's Kumamoto earthquake is still under way.

stories.title: 皇居三の丸尚蔵館がきょう全面開館 2期棟が加わり展示面積は約8倍、若冲の全30幅も
stories.summary: 皇居東御苑の皇居三の丸尚蔵館が、2期にわたる建て替えを終えて11月3日に全面開館しました。展示室は3室になり、展示面積は以前の約8倍に広がります。
body: 皇室に伝わった美術品を収める皇居三の丸尚蔵館（東京・千代田区、皇居東御苑内）が、文化の日の11月3日に全面開館しました。前日の2日には報道陣に館内が公開されています。旧館を2期に分けて建て替える事業で、2023年11月3日に第1期棟が開館して現在の名前に改められ、旧館の跡地に建てられた第2期棟が今回加わりました。
全面開館で展示室は3室になり、展示面積は旧施設の約160m2から約8倍の約1300m2に広がりました。管理運営は宮内庁から国立文化財機構に移っています。隣には同時に「大手休憩所」が開業し、皇居で初めてのカフェが入ります。
開館を記念する特別展「皇居の至宝―美いづるところ」は2027年1月24日まで開かれます。伊藤若冲の《動植綵絵》全30幅がそろって並ぶほか、正倉院宝物が皇居で初めて一般に公開されます。
stories.commentary: 160m2から、約1300m2へ。旧館の展示室は、ちょっと広めのコンビニくらいの大きさでした。皇室に伝わった名品が数千点あるのに、一度に見せられるのはほんのひと握り。それを、建物を2回に分けて建て替えることで広げたのが今回の事業なんです。実は、この「2回に分ける」が肝でした。1期棟を先に建てて収蔵品の引っ越し先をつくり、空いた旧館を壊して、その跡に2期棟を建てる。美術品は預ける倉庫を探すのも大変なので、お店を開けたまま改装するような段取りになるんですよね。場所が皇居の中だというのも、ほかの美術館にはない条件です。石垣とお濠に囲まれた東御苑に、新しい建物を目立たせすぎずに置く必要がありました。若冲の30幅が一つの部屋に並ぶのは、この広さがあってこそです。特別展の会期は、2027年1月24日までです。
briefing: 設計は日建設計が担当しています。宮内庁は2016年に「三の丸尚蔵館増築・改修ほか設計業務」を同社に発注しており、2期にわたる建て替えを同じ設計者が通して手がけました。
第1期棟は2023年11月3日に開館し、このとき名前が「三の丸尚蔵館」から「皇居三の丸尚蔵館」に改められました。今回の全面開館は、そこからちょうど3年後の同じ文化の日にあたります。
特別展では、皇居で初めてとなる正倉院宝物の一般公開も行われます。

sources.name: 皇居三の丸尚蔵館（公式）

hojosen.title: 動かしながら建て替える
hojosen.body: 収蔵品を抱えたまま美術館を建て替えるには、先に新しい収蔵庫をつくって引っ越し、空いた建物を壊すという手順が必要になります。今回も1期棟の完成から全面開館まで約3年をかけました。博物館や病院のように機能を止められない建物の更新では、この段階的な建て替えがよく使われます。

hojosen.title: 宮内庁から国立へ
hojosen.body: 三の丸尚蔵館はもともと宮内庁の施設でしたが、建て替えに合わせて管理運営が国立文化財機構に移されました。皇室の美術品を「国の文化財」として公開していく体制に切り替わったといえます。

stories.sourceName: 皇居三の丸尚蔵館（公式）

en.title: Tokyo's imperial art museum Sannomaru Shozokan fully opens with eight times the gallery space
en.summary: Sannomaru Shozokan, the museum of the Japanese imperial family's art collection in the East Gardens of the Imperial Palace in Tokyo, fully opened on November 3 after a two-phase rebuild. It now has three galleries and about eight times the exhibition space it had before.
body: The Sannomaru Shozokan (the Museum of the Imperial Collections), which holds art passed down through Japan's imperial family, fully opened on November 3, Culture Day, a national holiday. The museum is in Tokyo's Chiyoda Ward, inside the East Gardens of the Imperial Palace, the part of the palace grounds in central Tokyo that is open to the public. The press was shown inside the day before, on November 2.

The project replaced the old museum in two phases. The Phase 1 building opened on November 3, 2023, when the museum took its current name, and the Phase 2 building, built on the site of the old museum, has now been added.

With the full opening, the museum has three galleries, and its exhibition space has grown about eightfold, from about 160 m² (1,700 sq ft) in the old facility to about 1,300 m² (14,000 sq ft). Management has moved from the Imperial Household Agency, the government body that handles the affairs of the imperial family, to the National Institutes for Cultural Heritage, which also runs the Tokyo and Kyoto National Museums. Next door, the Ote rest house opened at the same time, bringing the first cafe ever to the Imperial Palace.

A special exhibition on the treasures of the Imperial Palace marks the opening and runs until January 24, 2027. It brings together all 30 scrolls of Colorful Realm of Living Beings, the celebrated set of bird-and-flower paintings by the eighteenth-century Kyoto painter Ito Jakuchu. It is also the first time treasures from the Shosoin, the eighth-century imperial storehouse in Nara, have been shown to the public at the Imperial Palace.
en.commentary: From 160 m² (1,700 sq ft) to about 1,300 m² (14,000 sq ft). The old galleries were about the size of a slightly roomy convenience store, the kind of konbini you find on every corner in Japan. The imperial family's collection includes thousands of masterpieces, yet only a tiny handful could be shown at any one time. This project widened that window by rebuilding the museum in two rounds. Here's the thing: splitting it in two was the key. First you build Phase 1 so the collection has somewhere to move. Then you tear down the emptied old building and put Phase 2 on its site. Finding a warehouse to store artworks is hard in itself, so the whole thing ends up like renovating a shop while keeping it open, right? The location adds a condition no other museum faces: it's inside the Imperial Palace. In the East Gardens, surrounded by stone walls and moats, the new building had to sit quietly without standing out too much. Jakuchu's 30 scrolls can hang together in one room only because of this extra space. The special exhibition runs until January 24, 2027.
briefing: The design is by Nikken Sekkei. The Imperial Household Agency commissioned the firm in 2016 for design work on the extension and renovation of the Sannomaru Shozokan, so the same architect saw the two-phase rebuild through from start to finish.

The Phase 1 building opened on November 3, 2023, and at that point the museum's Japanese name gained the prefix Kokyo, meaning Imperial Palace. The full opening falls exactly three years later, on the same Culture Day.
The special exhibition also includes the first public showing of Shosoin treasures at the Imperial Palace.

hojosen.title: Rebuilding while staying open
hojosen.body: To rebuild a museum while it still holds its collection, you first build new storage, move everything in, and then demolish the emptied building. Here, about three years passed between the completion of the Phase 1 building and the full opening. This kind of phased rebuild is common when updating buildings that can't simply shut down, such as museums and hospitals.

hojosen.title: From palace agency to national body
hojosen.body: The Sannomaru Shozokan was originally a facility of the Imperial Household Agency, but its management moved to the National Institutes for Cultural Heritage along with the rebuild. It marks a shift to a setup that presents the imperial family's art to the public as national cultural property.

namesEn.皇居三の丸尚蔵館（公式）: The Museum of the Imperial Collections, Sannomaru Shozokan (official)

stories.title: 日建連と不動協、現場の休み方で溝 ゼネコンは「土日閉所」、不動産側は「シフト制」
stories.summary: ゼネコンの日建連と不動産大手の不動協が、担い手確保を巡る協議の中身を明らかにしました。育成費の負担では歩み寄る一方、休日の取り方では意見が分かれています。
body: ゼネコンなどでつくる日本建設業連合会（日建連）と、不動産大手が加盟する不動産協会（不動協）が、建設業の担い手確保を巡る協議の状況を10月下旬に明らかにしました。両団体は今年、業界の枠を超えた初めての協議体を設けており、実務者レベルの幹事会で工期や働き方などの課題を話し合ってきました。
協議では、技能者などの担い手を育てる費用を、発注者である不動産業界も負担する仕組みを検討することについて、前向きな意見が出ました。一方で現場の休日の確保では、不動協が工期が延びるのを抑えるために交代で休む「シフト制」を提案したのに対し、日建連は交代要員の確保や引き継ぎの負担を理由に、現場ごと土日に閉める「土日閉所」を基本とする立場を示し、議論は平行線となっています。
両団体は2027年春をめどに対応方針を取りまとめる予定です。方針に沿って各社が任意で取り組むほか、両団体で政府に要望することも想定しています。
stories.commentary: 同じ「週休2日」でも、休み方は二通りあります。現場ごと土日に門を閉めるか、人を入れ替えながら現場は毎日動かすか。不動産会社の側から見ると、シフト制のほうが工期は延びにくいんです。ビルの完成が1カ月遅れれば、テナントの入居も家賃収入もそのぶん後ろにずれますから。ただ、ゼネコンの言い分にも理由があります。工事現場の仕事は、コンビニのレジ打ちのように誰が入っても同じ、とはいきません。昨日どこまで鉄筋を組んだか、どの職人さんに何を頼んだかを、毎日引き継ぐのは、想像以上に大変じゃないですか。もう一つ大事なのは、職人さん側の事情です。現場が土日に閉まっていれば、家族と休みを合わせられる。若い人に選ばれる仕事にするには、ここが効くと思うんです。工期とお金を出すのは発注者、人を集めて現場を回すのは施工者。休みの形を決めるのは、どちらなんでしょうね。
briefing: 日建連は2024年1月にも、時間外労働の上限規制が建設業に適用される「2024年問題」を前に、不動協に適正な工期の設定など働き方改革への協力を求めていました。今回の協議体は、その要請から一歩進んで、発注者と受注者が同じ席で課題を話し合う場です。
協議体では担い手確保のほか、建設費の上昇や供給力の確保など複数のテーマを扱っています。2026年度中には外国人材の獲得などをテーマに幹事会をさらに数回開く予定です。
取りまとめる方針には法的な拘束力はなく、各社が任意で取り組む形が想定されています。発注者側の費用負担がどこまで実際の契約に反映されるかが、今後の焦点になります。

hojosen.title: 発注者が変わる番
hojosen.body: 建設現場の週休2日はこれまで、主に国や自治体の公共工事で、工期や費用に休日分を見込む形で広がってきました。民間工事では発注者の理解が欠かせず、マンションやオフィスビルの大口発注者である不動産大手の姿勢が鍵を握ってきました。

hojosen.title: 「閉所」と「休日」の違い
hojosen.body: 建設業界では、技能者一人ひとりが週2日休む「週休2日（交代）」と、現場そのものを週2日閉める「4週8閉所」を区別して扱います。閉所のほうが休みが確実に取れる反面、工期は延びやすく、どちらを基本にするかで発注者と施工者の利害が分かれます。

en.title: Japan's contractors and developers split over how construction sites should take days off
en.summary: Nikkenren, the lobby group for Japan's general contractors, and Fudokyo, the association of major real estate developers, have disclosed where their talks on securing construction workers stand. They are moving closer on sharing training costs but disagree on how sites should take days off.
body: The Japan Federation of Construction Contractors (Nikkenren), the main lobby group for Japan's general contractors, and the Real Estate Companies Association of Japan (Fudokyo), whose members include the country's largest developers, disclosed in late October where their talks on securing the construction workforce stand. This year the two groups set up their first-ever forum spanning the two industries, and a working-level steering committee has been discussing issues such as construction schedules and working conditions.

In the talks, there were positive views on considering a system in which the real estate industry, as the client that commissions the buildings, also shares the cost of training skilled tradespeople and other workers. On securing days off at construction sites, however, the two sides remain far apart. Fudokyo proposed a shift system, in which workers take turns having days off, to keep schedules from stretching out. Nikkenren, citing the difficulty of finding replacement workers and the burden of handovers, took the position that the basic approach should be closing entire sites on Saturdays and Sundays.
The two groups plan to draw up a policy by around spring 2027. Member companies would follow it on a voluntary basis, and the groups also expect to make joint requests to the government.
en.commentary: Even under the same goal of two days off a week, there are two ways to take them. You either lock the gates of the whole site on weekends, or you keep the site running every day and rotate the people. From a developer's point of view, the shift system keeps schedules from slipping. If a building is finished a month late, tenant move-ins and rental income get pushed back by that much. But the contractors have their reasons too. Construction work isn't like running the register at a convenience store, where anyone who steps in does the same job. Handing over, every single day, how far the rebar got yesterday and which tradesperson was asked to do what is harder than you'd imagine, isn't it? One more important point is the workers' side. If the site is closed on weekends, they can line up their days off with their families. I think that's what will count in making this a job young people choose. The client sets the schedule and puts up the money; the builder gathers the people and runs the site. So which of them should decide what days off look like?
briefing: In January 2024, ahead of the so-called 2024 problem, when caps on overtime work were set to start applying to the construction industry, Nikkenren had already asked Fudokyo to cooperate on work-style reform, including setting reasonable construction schedules. The new forum goes a step further, bringing clients and contractors to the same table to discuss these issues.

Besides securing workers, the forum covers several topics, including rising construction costs and maintaining the industry's capacity to build. The steering committee plans to meet several more times during fiscal 2026 (Japan's fiscal year runs April to March) on themes such as recruiting foreign workers.
The policy will not be legally binding; companies are expected to follow it voluntarily. The next question is how far the clients' share of costs will actually be reflected in real contracts.

hojosen.title: The client's turn to change
hojosen.body: Two days off a week at construction sites has spread so far mainly through public works commissioned by national and local governments, which build the days off into schedules and budgets. In private projects, the client's understanding is essential, so the stance of the big developers, the major clients for condominiums and office buildings, has been key.

hojosen.title: Site closures vs. days off
hojosen.body: Japan's construction industry distinguishes between two days off a week on a rotating basis, where each worker takes two days off weekly, and closing sites eight days every four weeks, where the site itself shuts two days a week. Closures make days off more certain but tend to lengthen schedules, and which one becomes the norm is where the interests of clients and contractors split.

stories.title: 竹中工務店が「宇宙建築推進室」を新設 月面インフラや自律施工の技術開発を本格化
stories.summary: 竹中工務店が11月1日付で技術本部に「宇宙建築推進室」を設けました。宇宙での居住空間の設計や、人がいなくても進む施工技術などの開発を担います。
body: 竹中工務店は11月1日付で、技術本部に「宇宙建築推進室」を設置しました。宇宙建築の事業に経営資源を継続して投じるための、本格的な推進体制として位置づけています。
推進室は、宇宙での居住空間の設計・開発、人がその場にいなくても機械が工事を進める自律施工の技術、月面のインフラ整備などに関する技術開発を進めます。JAXA（宇宙航空研究開発機構）や海外の機関との連携も進める方針です。
同社ではこれまで、社内の有志による「竹中宇宙建築タスクフォース」が関連技術の開発や産学官の連携を担ってきました。新しい推進室は、この活動を発展させ、会社として宇宙建築の事業に責任を持つ組織となります。
stories.commentary: 月の上には、職人さんも重機のオペレーターもいません。地球からは約38万km、資材を運ぶだけでも大変です。だから宇宙建築では、「人がいなくても建つ」技術が真ん中に来るんです。たとえるなら、ロボット掃除機に家を建ててもらうようなもの。指示を受けた機械が、自分で地面を均したり、ブロックを積んだりする世界です。実は、この技術は地上の現場にもそのまま返ってきます。職人さんが足りない、夜間や危ない場所での作業を減らしたい。宇宙で鍛えた自律施工は、そうした地上の悩みにもそのまま効くはずなんです。もう一つは、暮らしの質です。狭い宇宙の居住空間で、どう窓を取り、どう光や緑を感じてもらうか。これは、住宅を設計するときの悩みとよく似ています。有志の集まりが、会社の正式な部署になる。宇宙建築も、そういう段階に入ったんだと思います。
briefing: 同社は2024年度から、東京大学、九州大学、JAXAが共同で進める月面ベースキャンプの研究開発に参画しています。宇宙で野菜を育てて食べるなど、居住空間の快適さに関わる研究にも取り組んできました。
国土交通省は文部科学省と連携し、月面での建設を見据えた「宇宙無人建設革新技術開発」を進めています。無人で施工する技術を地上の建設現場にも生かすことが狙いの一つです。
推進室の設置は、竹中工務店が10月に公表した11月1日付の機構改革の一つとして発表されました。前身のタスクフォースとは今後も連携しながら事業を進めます。

sources.name: デジタル建設ニュース
JAXA 有人宇宙技術部門

hojosen.title: ゼネコンと宇宙
hojosen.body: 国内の大手ゼネコンでは、月面での建設や居住を見据えた研究が少しずつ広がっています。国の無人建設の技術開発プロジェクトに参加する企業も多く、遠隔操作や自動化の技術は、まず地上の現場の人手不足対策として使われ始めています。

en.title: Takenaka Corporation launches a space architecture office to develop lunar infrastructure
en.summary: Takenaka Corporation, one of Japan's five largest general contractors, set up a Space Architecture Promotion Office in its technology division on November 1. It will develop designs for living spaces in space and construction technology that works without people on site.
body: Takenaka Corporation, one of Japan's five largest general contractors, established a Space Architecture Promotion Office within its technology division on November 1. The company describes it as a full-fledged setup for continuing to invest management resources in the space architecture business.

The office will develop technology for designing living spaces in space, for autonomous construction, in which machines carry out the work without people present at the site, and for building infrastructure on the Moon. It also plans to work more closely with JAXA (the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) and with organizations overseas.

Until now, this work had been handled by the Takenaka Space Architecture Task Force, a volunteer group of employees that developed related technology and built partnerships with industry, academia and government. The new office builds on that activity and becomes the unit that takes corporate responsibility for the space architecture business.
en.commentary: On the Moon, there are no tradespeople and no heavy-equipment operators. It's about 380,000 km (236,000 miles) from Earth, and just getting materials there is a huge job. That's why technology that lets things get built without people sits at the center of space architecture. Think of it as asking a robot vacuum to build your house. Machines take instructions, then level the ground and stack blocks on their own. Here's the interesting part: this technology comes straight back to construction sites on Earth. We're short on tradespeople, and we want less work at night and in dangerous places. Autonomous construction honed in space should help with exactly those problems here on the ground. The other part is quality of life. In a cramped living space in space, how do you place the windows, and how do you let people feel light and greenery? That's very similar to the questions you wrestle with when designing a house. A volunteer group becomes an official department of the company. I think space architecture has entered that stage.
briefing: Since fiscal 2024, the company has taken part in research and development on a lunar base camp jointly led by the University of Tokyo, Kyushu University and JAXA. It has also worked on research into the comfort of living spaces, such as growing and eating vegetables in space.

The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) is working with the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) on a program to develop innovative technology for unmanned construction in space, with construction on the Moon in mind. One of its aims is to apply unmanned construction technology to building sites on Earth as well.
The new office was announced as part of an organizational restructuring, effective November 1, that Takenaka disclosed in October. The office will keep working with the task force that preceded it.

hojosen.title: General contractors in space
hojosen.body: Among Japan's major general contractors, research aimed at building and living on the Moon is gradually spreading. Many companies take part in the national program for unmanned construction technology, and remote-control and automation technology is first being put to use at construction sites on Earth to deal with labor shortages.

stories.title: 改正建築基準法施行令がきのう施行 資材が足りないときに備え「型式適合認定」に新たな類型
stories.summary: 住宅の円滑な供給を目的に、改正建築基準法施行令が11月1日に施行されました。型式適合認定の拡充に加え、採光・防火・危険物の規制も合理化されます。
body: 国土交通省が9月11日に閣議決定し、9月16日に公布した「建築基準法施行令の一部を改正する政令」が、11月1日に施行されました。建物の安全性を保ちながら、住宅の円滑な供給や新しい設備の導入を後押しすることが目的です。
柱になるのは型式適合認定制度の拡充です。これまでの「建築物全体」「建築設備を除いた建築物」「建築設備」の3つの類型に、「構造耐力に関する規定」への適合を対象とする類型が加わりました。特定の建築資材が手に入りにくくなった場合でも、構造耐力の審査の省略を受けたうえで、代わりの資材に関わる部分だけを個別に確認審査する運用ができるようになります。
あわせて3つの規制も見直されました。児童福祉施設などのうち、利用者の滞在時間が短く衛生上の支障がないと国土交通大臣が定める施設は、採光規制の対象から外れます。一定の防耐火性能をもつ建物は防火・避難規制の対象から除く道が開かれ、用途地域ごとの危険物の総量規制では、大臣の基準に合う燃料用ガス設備が除外されます。
stories.commentary: レシピごと、国の検定を通しておく。型式適合認定は、そんな仕組みなんです。同じ間取り・同じ構造の家をたくさん建てるハウスメーカーは、あらかじめ「この型なら基準に合っている」と認めてもらっておくと、一棟ごとの確認申請で審査の一部を省けます。困るのは、材料が一つ手に入らなくなったときですよね。これまでは、レシピの一部を差し替えるだけで、検定済みという前提が崩れかねませんでした。今回の改正で、構造の部分だけを型として認めてもらい、差し替えた資材のところだけ個別に審査を受ける、という使い分けができるようになります。実は、ここで省けるのは審査の手間であって、現場の確認ではありません。認定どおりに建っているかを見る目は、むしろ大事になると思うんです。認定の類型は、これで4つになりました。
briefing: 政令は9月11日に閣議決定、9月16日に公布されました。関係する告示や建築基準法施行規則の改正も、10月末に公布して11月1日に施行する予定と案内されていました。
採光規制と防火・避難規制の適用除外は、いずれも国土交通大臣が定める基準を満たす場合に限られます。具体的な基準は告示で示されるため、実務での判断には告示の確認が欠かせません。
危険物の総量規制の見直しは、圧縮ガスや可燃性ガスを燃料とする設備の導入を後押しする狙いがあります。住宅地を含む用途地域で、新しいエネルギー設備を置きやすくする措置です。

sources.name: ハウジング・トリビューン

hojosen.title: 型式認定と量産住宅
hojosen.body: 型式適合認定は、同じ仕様の住宅を繰り返し建てる事業者にとって、確認審査を効率化する仕組みとして使われてきました。一方で、仕様のどこかを変えると認定の前提が崩れるため、資材の調達先を変えにくいという面がありました。今回の類型追加は、その硬さを部分的にほぐす改正です。

hojosen.title: 続く規制の合理化
hojosen.body: 建築基準法まわりでは、2025年4月の4号特例の縮小のように審査を厳しくする改正と、手続きや規制を合理化する改正が並行して進んでいます。今回は後者で、安全性の基準そのものは下げずに、審査の進め方と適用範囲を見直す形です。

en.title: Japan's revised building rules take effect, adding a new type approval route for material shortages
